=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 161 (the Helpers intro sentence about git commands) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The live copy still reads "check the branch state in a separate call" — the OLD wording that pre-dates the review-round-1 fix.
  WHY: an `/implement-plan-claude` stage session reading the live copy has no concrete allowlisted command named for the "separate call" verification step. The session can still pick any chained form (`git status -sb | head -3`, `git status -sb; git log --oneline -3`, etc.), the chained call matches no `permissions.allow` rule, and the Auto-mode classifier denies it as `[Modify Shared Resources]` — the exact denial mode issue #5293 documents and the PR title claims to remove.
- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md: line 46 (step 5 "Fix it." sentence) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Same divergence as above. The live copy reads "check the branch state in a separate call" while the workflow-templates twin reads "check the branch state with `git status -sb`, and `HEAD` with `git rev-parse HEAD`, each run as its own Bash call with nothing piped or chained to it."
  WHY: a `/fix-claude-pr` fixer session reading the live copy has no concrete allowlisted command named for the verification step and can pick a chained form the Auto-mode classifier will deny. The same Auto-mode `[Modify Shared Resources]` denial mode the PR title claims to fix recurs.
- tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py (test_template_parity parametrized over NAMES at lines 18 and 46) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: All four byte-equality contracts compare the live and template copies.
  WHY: The two copies differ at line 161 of implement-plan-claude.md and line 46 of fix-claude-pr.md (the four `git status -sb` / `git rev-parse HEAD` phrases appear only in the twin), so every one of these parity tests will fail in CI.
- changelog.d/5293-unchained-git-sync-calls.md | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment describes a state that the live `.claude/commands/` copies do not actually contain.
  WHY: `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` folds this fragment into `CHANGELOG.md` verbatim at release time without re-reading the source files, so consumers reading the assembled changelog will be told a behavior the live copy does not deliver.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (live) and .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md (live) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR's stated purpose (issue #5293) is to remove the Auto-mode `[Modify Shared Resources]` denial the chained-git pattern produces, but the concrete guidance is only in the workflow-templates twins.
  WHY: The Auto-mode classifier denial mode the PR title promises to remove still recurs on the live copy. The protection lives only on the twin files, which a `/implement-plan-claude` stage session or `/fix-claude-pr` fixer session does not read. The PR ships an effectively absent fix.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description and the lesson "[source:intervention] Guidance that tells an unattended session to do something 'in a separate call' must name the exact allowlisted command to run alone (for example `git status -sb`), or reviewers flag it and the session may pick a piped form no allow rule matches" together demand that the live `.claude/commands/` copies contain the concrete `git status -sb` (and `git rev-parse HEAD` for `fix-claude-pr.md`) wording — the file an unattended session actually reads.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:161 and .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 (the live copies, mirroring the workflow-templates twin edits the PR already made).

The live copy at .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:161 reads "check the branch state in a separate call" — the pre-fix phrasing — and the live copy at .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 reads "check the branch state in a separate call" likewise. The PR's progress log notes "A second twin-sync copies the two twins into `.claude/commands/`" but that second twin-sync has not landed in this PR. test_git_commands_run_unchained reads only `TEMPLATE_COMMANDS / ...`, so it cannot catch this gap by itself.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
